clue.text: Good ear features — they are rounded

parts.note: the fleshy lower parts of the ear are its lobes

explanation.surface: Someone praises a person's fine-looking ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ear features' reads as part of a compliment, but it is just a synonym for the lobes.
explanation.definitionFit: Spheres such as balls and planets are the classic rounded objects, so the plural matches 'they'.

clue.text: Drug supplied by naughty lad outside work

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters wrap around the next piece
naughty suggests the letters of lad misbehave and fall out of order

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A mischievous boy is caught dealing drugs with work on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated name is written with its initial L separate; 'supplied by' is a link. The anagram of the boy's letters goes round the opus abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A medication given for Parkinson's disease, a precursor of the brain chemical dopamine.

clue.text: Stop working in short holiday away from Oxford?

parts.note: a break is a brief holiday
a student who has left the university is said to have gone down from Oxford

explanation.surface: A student takes a mini-holiday off campus.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge students 'go down' when they leave for the vacation or for good.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun-style phrase for a machine or person ceasing to function; a car's failure is a classic example.

clue.text: Army prisoner could undermine this ultimately?

definitions.text: Army prisoner could undermine this ultimately?

parts.words: Army prisoner could undermine this ultimately?
parts.note: a captured soldier might eventually tunnel under the walls of the German prisoner-of-war camp holding him

explanation.surface: A captured soldier plots to sabotage his captors in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undermine' is meant literally: digging a tunnel beneath the camp, as in famous wartime escapes.
explanation.definitionFit: A German camp for captured servicemen in the Second World War, the scene of tunnel escapes.

clue.text: Left-winger with frivolous warning

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist, someone on the political left
light means lacking seriousness, as in light reading

explanation.surface: A socialist issues a jokey caution.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic signal ordering drivers to stop, and figuratively any sign of danger.

clue.text: MPs perhaps disturbed by inveterate press

indicators.note: disturbed suggests the letters of the following words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Members of Parliament are upset by persistent newspaper hounding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' shuffles the fifteen letters of INVETERATE PRESS; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Parliament are an example of elected delegates, flagged by 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Actress has choice of food that's full-flavoured

parts.note: a diet is the selection of food a person eats
rich food is heavy and full of flavour

explanation.surface: A performer picks a hearty, flavoursome meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Marlene Dietrich was a German-American film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was a famous film star of the 1930s, such as in The Blue Angel.

clue.text: River business — try to escape from it

indicators.note: to escape from it says the word try gets out of the longer word

parts.note: industry is commerce or business activity
taken as written

explanation.surface: A firm's employee tries to break free of the business world.
explanation.walkthrough: The river runs through Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: A major Asian waterway flowing from Tibet through Pakistan to the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Messenger is alcoholic almost, one inclined to overindulgence

indicators.note: almost says the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: hard drink is strong alcoholic liquor
a binger eats or drinks to excess in bouts

explanation.surface: A courier is nearly a drunk and prone to excess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; 'almost' trims HARD to HAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald or forerunner announcing something to come, so a bearer of news.

clue.text: Not against old lover having enough say

parts.note: for is the opposite of against
an ex is a former partner
ample means plenty, enough

explanation.surface: A former partner, given enough of a say, turns supportive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like a verb or noun at the end, but it is the definition in its 'for instance' sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both introduce an illustration: 'take, say, Paris' means take Paris as an instance.

clue.text: Beginning or end of dream in corporate bedroom

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A dream starts or finishes in a shared sleeping room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning' and 'end of' both act on 'dream', with OR between them; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormitory is a shared sleeping room used by a group, hence corporate in the collective sense.

clue.text: 'Footballer has quiet time' — where might you see that? (But not here!)

parts.note: a back is a defender in football
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A sports headline about a player resting, with a joke that it isn't printed here.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted line is a sports headline, found on the last page of a newspaper; 'But not here!' teases that this is the crossword page.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers traditionally put sports stories on their final page, so a footballer headline appears there.

clue.text: Country that could trouble USA, sir!

indicators.note: could trouble suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone warns a superior that a nation could cause the Americans difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest nation on Earth, spanning Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Go away from fire wasting little time

indicators.note: wasting says something is lost from the word for fire

parts.note: to shoot is to fire a gun
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone retreats from a blaze without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' signals the abbreviation; 'wasting' drops it.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection used to drive off an animal or person, an order to depart.

clue.text: Dispose of a shire right here!

definitions.text: Dispose of a shire right here!

indicators.note: dispose in its sense of arrange or set out tells you to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to sell off a heavy draught animal at the right venue.
explanation.walkthrough: A shire is a big English draught horse. 'Dispose' rearranges OFASHIRE plus R; the whole clue also says where you would sell one.
explanation.definitionFit: A market where horses such as shires are bought and sold, the place to dispose of one.

clue.text: Eastern objects, about a hundred artistic items

indicators.note: about says the word for objects goes round the next piece

parts.note: things are objects
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Oriental artefacts, about a hundred of them, are on display.
explanation.definitionFit: Prints made from engraved metal plates are works of art, such as Rembrandt's.

clue.text: Run up debts, showing no concern to learn?

parts.note: to incur a debt is to run it up
IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts

explanation.surface: Someone piling up debts, apparently untroubled by the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking curiosity, with no wish to find things out, matches no concern to learn.

clue.text: Principal dealt with a rebellious fighter, a source of worry

parts.note: a head is the principal of a school
Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary guerrilla

explanation.surface: A headteacher tackles a troublesome rebel pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealt with' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a problem or nuisance, a cause of anxiety rather than a literal pain.

clue.text: Most open row interrupting celebratory party

indicators.note: interrupting says the word for row breaks into the party word

parts.note: a fest is a festival or celebration
a rank is a row or line

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks up a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'cow' in the surface, but here it means a line, as in rank and file.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of frank, candid and outspoken, so most open in manner.

clue.text: Worry when vehicle has sign of no petrol?

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
E for empty is marked on a fuel gauge

explanation.surface: Anxiety strikes when the fuel gauge reads empty.
explanation.walkthrough: Petrol is British for gasoline.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, concern or anxiety, as in 'without a care in the world'.

clue.text: Supplies rushed aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard says the rushing word sits inside the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
tore means rushed, as in tore down the road

explanation.surface: Provisions are hurriedly loaded on a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocks or provisions kept for use, especially on a voyage.

clue.text: Skilled in poetic style

definitions.meaning: well informed and practised in a subject
written in metre and lines rather than prose

explanation.surface: Someone is adept at writing in a lyrical way.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means experienced, as in versed in law, and also put into lines of poetry.

clue.text: Tot caught hugging a tree

indicators.note: hugging says the preceding letters embrace the next piece

parts.note: to tot up is to sum
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A toddler is caught clinging to a trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a child, but it means a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub or small tree whose berries give a tart spice in Middle Eastern cooking.

clue.text: What can indicate disapproval, love, anger? All in a teacher's role

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound of disapproval
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
rage is fury

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster's job seems to be all scolding, affection and temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All in' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The position or work of a private instructor, the job of one who tutors.

clue.text: Birds emerging from these eggs the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Chicks hatch from eggs in an odd manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals the run of letters inside 'these eggs', read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Large waterfowl, the plural of goose, here birds coming out of shells.

clue.text: Still gripped by magical moments

indicators.note: gripped by says the letters are held within the following words

explanation.surface: A feeling of stillness held during enchanting times.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaceful and untroubled, without wind or movement, as in still water.

clue.text: No cost ever worked out for motorists' temporary requirements?

indicators.note: worked out suggests the letters are reworked into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Drivers are promised something free of charge, if they can figure it out.
explanation.walkthrough: These are British insurance documents giving interim cover before the full policy arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim insurance certificates that drivers need until their full policy document is issued.

clue.text: Holly had these insects

definitions.meaning: Buddy Holly's backing band was the ...

explanation.surface: A holly bush crawling with bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Holly is not the plant but the rock and roll singer Buddy Holly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the singer's band and the chirping insects share one name.

clue.text: Having a band, Salvationists must have basic accommodation

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army
a shed is a simple hut

explanation.surface: A Salvation Army brass band needs a rough place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians, which fits the Salvation Army, but here it is a strip of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing a sash, a band of fabric worn across the body or round the waist.
